name: Balaam
description: Prophet living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness

points: Sacrificing animals was not solely a thing pertaining to Israel; sacrificing for sin is what pertained to Israel. All the ancient nations of old sacrificed animals when they worshipped their gods, so Balak and Balaam offering bullocks and rams on altars was nothing new to them.
Offering animals on altars had been done since the time of Adam. It was commonplace in that time, so do not be confused at why Balaam keeps calling for altars and offerings through this chapter.

note.label: Numbers 23: How Shall I Curse, Whom God Hath Not Cursed?

points: When Balaam saw that it pleased the Lord to bless Israel, he went not to seek enchantments, and the spirit of God came upon him. Do not be confused at the spirit of God coming on a man of another nation: all the spirits belong to the Most High, and He can do what He wants with any of them.

That does not make the other nations prophets. Prophets are raised up of the sons of Israel; the Lord used Balaam for one specific purpose, to show the nations there is nothing they can do against Israel when the Lord is on our side, and to have Moses write it down in a book.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

points: Balaam dealt with enchantments, which lets us know he is a witch, a soothsayer, a diviner. When it says the spirit of God came upon him, notice the little s: this is on the left hand side; it is not the Holy Spirit coming on Balaam.

Balak's anger was kindled and he smote his hands together: I thought to promote thee unto great honour, but lo, the Lord hath kept thee back from honour. That was Satan speaking through Balak, trying to entice Balaam with honor to curse Israel.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

points: And Balaam rose up and returned to his place, and Balak also went his way; they parted.

note.label: Numbers 24: A Star out of Jacob and the Latter Days

points: Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword. Balaam was a soothsayer, a diviner; he was a witch, so to speak.

These caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor. The Lord would not allow Balaam to curse us, but Balaam told Balak: I can't curse them, but I can tell you how to make them fall. How? Whoredom.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

points: These women caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor. Balaam took it upon himself to send the women of the other nations to Israel, and it caused the people to go into fornication, and the Lord began putting them to death, over twenty and four thousand, in the history of Numbers 25.
The reason for the ban: Ammon and Moab met not Israel with bread and with water in the way when they came forth out of Egypt, and hired Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor to curse them.

The history is in Numbers: Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, was sore afraid because the people were many, and sent the elders of Moab and Midian with the rewards of divination to call Balaam to curse Israel.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

points: Nevertheless the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam, but turned the curse into a blessing, because the Lord thy God loveth thee; therefore Israel was never to seek their peace nor their prosperity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

points: With the princes of Midian, Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword. This is the same Balaam from Numbers 22, the one whose ass saw the angel standing there to kill him when he could not see it himself. He was the one going after the lust of greed, and he ended up getting put to death.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

points: Then Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and warred against Israel, and sent and called Balaam the son of Beor to curse Israel; that is Numbers 22, read only days before this class.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: But I would not hearken unto Balaam; therefore he blessed you still: so I delivered you out of his hand.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: On that day they read in the books of Moses and found written that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever, because they met not Israel with bread and water but hired Balaam against them to curse them, and the Most High turned the curse into a blessing.

note.label: Nehemiah 13: Cleansing the People, the Sabbath, and the Strange Wives

points: O my people, remember now what Balak king of Moab consulted, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him, that ye may know the righteousness of the Lord.

note.label: Micah 6: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee

points: Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain: they hate their brothers and sisters. And ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward: money. And perished in the gainsaying of Core: they want position, they want rank, they want preeminence.

note.label: Traitors and Their Exquisite Subtlety: The Judas Iscariot Effect
